Foundations states the subject's structural facts and demonstrates each: the accounting equation
as an invariant, the debit-credit convention as the rule that preserves it transaction by
transaction, and the trial balance as the check that the invariant survived posting.

- **The accounting equation and double entry** — the invariant, the entry rule, worked
  transactions showing each preservation.
- **The trial balance** — striking it, reading it, and what it does and does not verify.

Opening pages landing next in this track.

## Prerequisites

Arithmetic and the willingness to check that entries balance. Every mechanic is shown on a worked
example before it is used anywhere else, so nothing must be taken on faith.

## What the track is for

Every later mechanic — adjusting entries, closing entries, statement construction — is an
application of the structural facts this track establishes. The track is also where the subject's
vocabulary is defined: debit and credit by their effect on the equation, not by rote; the trial
balance as an invariant check rather than a ritual.

## What the track is for

Every later mechanic — adjusting entries, closing entries, statement construction — applies the
structural facts this track establishes. It is also where the vocabulary is defined: debit and
credit by their effect on the equation's sides rather than by rote, and the trial balance as an
invariant check with a precise limit — it catches one-sided errors, not misclassified or missing
ones.

## Reading the worked examples

The examples are numbered transaction by transaction, and each entry shows both sides of the
equation moving. The recommendation is to cover the entry and predict it: the subject is learned
by producing entries, not by verifying them.

## The standard

Definitions precede use, every mechanic is demonstrated before it is generalised, and every
worked example balances — not as a flourish but as the subject's own verification. The pages keep
the invariant visible at each step rather than burying it under procedure.

## The Accounting Equation
URL: https://accounting.wyattau.com/1-foundations/1_the-accounting-equation/

<!-- Breadcrumb Schema for SEO -->
<script type="application/ld+json">
{
  "@context": "https://schema.org",
  "@type": "BreadcrumbList",
  "itemListElement": [{"name": "Home", "url": "https://wyattau.com"}, {"name": "accounting", "url": "https://accounting.wyattau.com"}, {"name": "1 Foundations", "url": "https://accounting.wyattau.com/1-foundations"}, {"name": "The Accounting Equation and Double Entry", "url": "https://accounting.wyattau.com/1-foundations/1_the-accounting-equation"}]
}
</script>

### 1. The Invariant

**Definition.** The **accounting equation** is

$$
\text{Assets} = \text{Liabilities} + \text{Equity}.
$$

It is not a formula to compute; it is a statement that must remain true after every recorded
event. Assets are what the entity controls of value; liabilities are outsiders' claims on it;
equity is the owners' residual claim — what remains for them after every outsider is paid. The
equation says the two ways of listing what the entity is worth (the things themselves; the claims
against them) agree. That agreement is the invariant the whole subject preserves.

### 2. Double Entry Preserves the Invariant

**Theorem 2.1.** If the accounting equation holds and a transaction is recorded as equal debits
and credits, the equation holds after the transaction.

**Proof.** Each account has a side (debit or credit) on which it increases. The convention,
derived below, is: assets and expenses increase on the debit side; liabilities, equity, and
revenues increase on the credit side. An entry posts amount $t$ to each of two accounts. Four
cases:

1. **Debit an asset, credit an asset** (e.g., buy inventory with cash): one asset rises by $t$,
   another falls by $t$. Total assets unchanged; both sides unchanged. Equation holds.
2. **Debit an asset, credit a liability or equity** (e.g., borrow cash; issue shares for cash):
   assets rise by $t$ and the right side rises by $t$. Both sides increase equally. Holds.
3. **Debit a liability or equity, credit an asset** (e.g., repay a loan with cash): the right
   side falls by $t$ and assets fall by $t$. Both sides decrease equally. Holds.
4. **Debit and credit both on the right side** (e.g., revenue earned on credit): a liability or
   revenue rises by $t$ and another falls by $t$. Right side net unchanged; assets unchanged.
   Holds.

Every entry is one of these four shapes (or the mirrored shapes with assets on the credit side —
same arithmetic). In every case the two sides move by equal amounts, so an equation that held
before the entry holds after it. By induction over all transactions, the invariant holds
forever. $\blacksquare$

### 3. Where the Debit-Credit Convention Comes From

The convention is not arbitrary; it is forced by the invariant. Choose: debits increase assets
(the subject's historical root is recording what is in the chest). Then for the equation to
balance, entries touching the right side must *increase* the right side on credits — because
when a credit also touches an asset, the asset rises by a debit, so the right side must rise by
a credit to keep pace. Revenues ultimately increase equity, so revenues increase on credits;
expenses reduce equity, so expenses increase on debits. Every rule students memorise is this
derivation.

### 4. The Trial Balance: The Invariant's Check

**Definition.** The **trial balance** lists every account's balance with total debits and total
credits.

**Theorem 4.1.** If every entry had equal debits and credits, the trial balance's two totals are
equal.

**Proof.** Each entry contributes the same amount $t$ to both totals. Summing over all entries,
both totals equal $\sum_{\text{entries}} t$. Equal. $\blacksquare$

The check has a precise limit, and knowing the limit is the skill: the trial balance catches
*one-sided* errors (a debit posted without its credit, or at a different amount). It does **not**
catch an entry posted to the wrong account (both sides correct, classification wrong), a missing
transaction (nothing posted, nothing to catch), or offsetting errors. A clean trial balance means
the invariant held; it does not mean the books are right.

### 5. Worked Example: Four Transactions

A new consultancy, recording four events:

<div class="table-wrap">

| # | Event | Entry (debit → credit) | Shape | Effect on equation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Owners invest \$10,000 cash | Cash \$10,000 → Equity \$10,000 | Case 2 | Both sides +10,000 |
| 2 | Borrow \$5,000 from the bank | Cash \$5,000 → Loan \$5,000 | Case 2 | Both sides +5,000 |
| 3 | Buy \$3,000 of equipment with cash | Equipment \$3,000 → Cash \$3,000 | Case 1 | Assets reshuffled |
| 4 | Pay \$800 cash for this month's rent | Rent (expense) \$800 → Cash \$800 | Case 2, via equity | Both sides −800 |

</div>

Check after each event:

- After 1: Assets \$10,000 = Liabilities \$0 + Equity \$10,000. ✓
- After 2: Assets \$15,000 = Liabilities \$5,000 + Equity \$10,000. ✓
- After 3: Assets \$15,000 (cash down \$3,000, equipment up \$3,000) = \$5,000 + \$10,000. ✓
- After 4: Assets \$14,200 = \$5,000 + (\$10,000 − \$800 expense). ✓

Every line balances because every entry was double-entry — Theorem 2.1 executing four times.

### 6. What This Page Sets Up

Revenue and expense accounts are temporary equity sub-accounts: they accumulate the period's
changes to equity, then are closed into it. That is why Case 2 covers "revenue earned on credit"
— the credit to revenue is a credit to a future piece of equity. The
[accounting cycle](/2-the-accounting-cycle/) runs this machinery across a full period, adding the
accrual principle's adjustments; the equation remains the invariant throughout.

### Self-test

1. Which of the four shapes is "receive an invoice for utilities, unpayed"? (Case 2 mirrored to
   expenses: debit the expense, credit a liability — the right side rises by the payable.)
2. Why does the trial balance catch a missing credit but not a missing transaction? (§4 —
   the totals compare what was posted; nothing posted leaves nothing to compare.)
3. State why expenses increase on the debit side. (§3 — expenses decrease equity; equity
   increases on credits; so their opposite, expenses, increase on debits.)

## The-Accounting-Cycle

---

## Index
URL: https://accounting.wyattau.com/2-the-accounting-cycle/

<!-- Breadcrumb Schema for SEO -->
<script type="application/ld+json">
{"@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": "BreadcrumbList", "itemListElement": [{"name": "Home", "url": "https://wyattau.com"}, {"name": "accounting", "url": "https://accounting.wyattau.com"}, {"name": "The Accounting Cycle", "url": "https://accounting.wyattau.com/2-the-accounting-cycle"}]}
</script>

The cycle is the subject executed end to end: transactions to journal, journal to ledger, ledger
to trial balance, adjustments justified by the accrual principle, adjusted trial balance, and the
four statements built from it — with the interlocks shown (income to retained earnings to balance
sheet, still balancing).

- **Journalising and posting** — the mechanics, worked on a running example company.
- **Adjusting entries** — accruals, deferrals, and depreciation, each justified by the accrual
  principle rather than asserted.
- **Statement construction** — the four statements built from the adjusted trial balance, with
  every number traceable.

Opening pages landing next in this track.

## Prerequisites

The [Foundations](/1-foundations/) track: the accounting equation, the entry rule, and the trial
balance. The cycle is those facts executed on a running company, period after period.

## What the track is for

The cycle is where the subject becomes a skill: a running company, a period, and the full
sequence from transaction to statements with nothing hidden. The pages use one example company
throughout, so each step's outputs are the next step's inputs — the way the work is actually
done.

## The running example

One example company runs the whole cycle: the same transactions flow from journal to ledger to
trial balance to adjustments to statements, so every step's outputs are the next step's inputs.
When the statements are built, every number traces back through the chain to a numbered
transaction — the traceability is the standard, and the pages maintain it.

## What the cycle is not

The cycle is not the hard part of accounting. The hard part is judgement: accrual estimates,
useful lives, allowance rates. The cycle exists to make the mechanical layer flawless so that the
judgement layer sits on statements that are internally consistent — and the pages keep the two
layers named separately.

## Overview

## About

This site provides free accounting notes built mechanics-first: the structural facts stated
precisely, every mechanic demonstrated on a worked example, and every worked example internally
consistent — the statements balance because the entries were posted correctly, and the pages show
the checking.

## The standard

Definitions precede use. Each new mechanic is shown on a worked example before it is generalised.
Adjusting entries are justified by the accrual principle rather than asserted. Where frameworks
differ (IFRS and US GAAP), the difference is named rather than averaged.

## The discipline framing

Accounting's reputation for tedium comes from being taught procedure-first, with the structure
revealed (if at all) at the end. These pages run the other way: the structure is page one, and
every procedure after it is a consequence. On that ordering the subject is short, and the
shortness is the point.

## Reading order

[Foundations](/1-foundations/) before [The Accounting Cycle](/2-the-accounting-cycle/). The
cycle pages assume the equation, the entry rule, and the trial balance as established in
Foundations, and their worked examples run a full period end to end — so reading them first is
reading the payoff without the setup.

## Frameworks

The pages teach the common core that IFRS and US GAAP share, and name the divergence where the
frameworks differ. Where a rule is convention rather than derivation, the site says so —
accounting standards are institutional facts, and the site's honesty about which facts are
institutional is part of its standard.

## Level

The level is the introductory financial-accounting sequence through the four statements and their
interlocks — the material of a first accounting course, done with the discipline of a first
physics course.

## The writing convention

Each mechanic appears three times: stated as a rule, worked on an example, and used in the next
example's input. The repetition is deliberate — the subject is learned by execution, and the
pages are structured so that execution is always against the stated rule rather than against a
remembered layout. Where students typically err (direction of adjustments, which statements a
closing entry touches), the page names the error at the point it would occur.

## The maintenance model

Content is checked by tooling on every change: depth minimums, frontmatter validity, link
integrity, and table formatting. The worked examples carry the site's standard — every number
traceable, every statement balanced — and the tooling enforces the formatting so the examples
stay readable.

## The network

This site is part of a network: exam-board sites for the school-facing business treatments,
subject sites (mathematics, physics, chemistry, computer science, economics, finance) for the
discipline-facing layer. Accounting's neighbours are economics for the transactions' context and
mathematics for the arithmetic's rigor; the links are maintained by tooling.

## How to report an error

Anything that looks wrong — a misclassified entry, an unbalanced example, a definition used
before it is stated — is worth reporting. The fix lands with the correction recorded, and a page
needing repeated patches gets a rewrite, because repeated patches mean the structure is wrong.

## Corrections

Misclassified entries, unbalanced examples, definitions used before they are stated — anything
found wrong is fixed and the correction recorded. A worked example that teaches a broken
mechanic is the site's worst failure mode, and the corrections policy exists because that
failure mode is only detectable by readers doing the work.

## The self-test convention

Self-test items ask for produced artifacts — the entry, the balance, the statement line — not
recognition of them. Producing is the skill the assessments examine and the job requires, and
producing is what the worked examples model.

## The glossary convention

Terms are defined at first use on every page — the glossary is recall, not introduction. The
definitions are written to be self-sufficient, because an accounting definition that requires a
chapter of context is a definition the reader cannot check at the moment of use, and
check-at-the-moment is this site's whole method.

## The first-page guarantee

Page one of every track states the invariants the whole track depends on. If a later page seems
to contradict one, trust the invariant and reread — and if the reread confirms the contradiction,
that is an error worth reporting under the corrections policy above.

## The corrections standard, restated

Balanced is necessary; correctly classified is sufficient; traceable is the standard. Corrections
hold all three.

## Glossary
URL: https://accounting.wyattau.com/glossary/

<!-- Breadcrumb Schema for SEO -->
<script type="application/ld+json">
{
  "@context": "https://schema.org",
  "@type": "BreadcrumbList",
  "itemListElement": [{"name": "Home", "url": "https://wyattau.com"}, {"name": "accounting", "url": "https://accounting.wyattau.com"}, {"name": "Glossary", "url": "https://accounting.wyattau.com/glossary"}]
}
</script>

- **Accrual principle** — revenue is recognised when earned and expenses when incurred, whether
  or not cash has moved. The gap between accrual and cash is why adjusting entries exist.
- **Accounting equation** — Assets = Liabilities + Equity. An invariant: every properly posted
  entry preserves it, because each entry's debits equal its credits.
- **Adjusting entries** — period-end entries recording earned-but-unrecorded revenue and
  incurred-but-unpaid expense (accruals), and allocated costs (deferrals, depreciation).
- **Closing entries** — period-end entries transferring revenue and expense balances to equity,
  resetting the temporary accounts so the next period starts clean.
- **Credit / Debit** — the two sides of an entry. Debits increase assets and expenses; credits
  increase liabilities, equity, and revenue. Memorising the rule is easier than deriving it: the
  sides are defined so that the equation's invariant is preserved.
- **Double entry** — every transaction posts equal debits and credits across at least two
  accounts. This is the mechanism that preserves the accounting equation transaction by
  transaction.
- **General ledger** — the collection of accounts to which journal entries are posted; the
  trial balance is struck from its balances.
- **Retained earnings** — the cumulative equity account absorbing each period's net income less
  distributions; the bridge from the income statement to the balance sheet.
- **Revenue recognition** — the rules deciding *when* performance has occurred enough to book
  revenue; the single most litigated area of the subject, and the reason the accrual principle
  needs standards rather than a slogan.
- **Trial balance** — the list of account balances with total debits and total credits. Equal
  totals verify the invariant held through posting; unequal totals prove an error.

Missing a term? The page using it defines it; the glossary collects the shared vocabulary.

## Conventions

Entries are shown in two-column journal form (debit account and amount, indented credit account
and amount). Statements appear in the standard order: income statement, statement of changes in
equity, balance sheet, cash flow statement — and the pages keep that order, because the
interlocks flow in it. Amounts are in a generic currency unit; nothing in the mechanics depends
on which.

## Statement terms

- **Balance sheet** — the statement of the accounting equation at a point in time: assets on one
  side, liabilities and equity on the other, equal by construction when the entries are right.
- **Income statement** — the period's revenues minus expenses, arriving at net income. Its
  bottom line flows into retained earnings, which is where it reaches the balance sheet.
- **Cash flow statement** — the period's cash movements, sorted into operating, investing, and
  financing. It is the reconciliation between accrual income and actual cash: net income plus
  the accrual reversals.

## How entries are ordered

Entries are alphabetical within the single list, because accounting's vocabulary is one shared
system rather than separate tracks. Each entry names the track that owns the term's deepest
treatment, so the glossary doubles as a subject map.

## The standard, restated

Every entry says what the thing is and what it does to the equation. That pairing — object and
effect — is the subject in miniature, and the glossary keeps the pairing visible even at
dictionary length.

- **Ledger account** — the running record of one asset, liability, equity, revenue, or expense
  category; its balance is what the trial balance reports and the statements consume.
- **Posting** — transferring a journal entry's amounts into the ledger accounts. Posting
  correctly preserves the invariant; posting to the wrong account preserves the totals but
  corrupts the statements — which is why the trial balance alone is not an audit.

- **Source document** — the invoice, receipt, or contract that authorises an entry; the evidence
  layer that keeps posting honest, and the reason "the books" are trusted in court.
- **Statement of changes in equity** — the bridge statement: opening equity, plus net income,
  minus distributions, plus contributions, equals closing equity. It is where the income
  statement's bottom line is delivered to the balance sheet.
- **Temporary account** — a revenue or expense account closed to zero at period end; its
  contents live on in equity, but its identity does not survive the closing entries.
- **Permanent account** — an asset, liability, or equity account whose balance carries forward.
  The distinction from temporary accounts is what the closing entries operate on.
- **Period** — the reporting interval the cycle runs on. The accrual principle allocates
  economic events to periods; without periods there would be no adjusting entries and no cycle.
- **Equity** — the owners' residual claim: assets minus liabilities. Not cash, not value — the
  accounting equation's balancing claim, and the statements' way of keeping score.
- **Contra account** — an account that subtracts from its parent (accumulated depreciation
  against equipment). Contras are how the statements show gross amounts and their offsets
  without losing either.

## Hub
URL: https://accounting.wyattau.com/hub/

Accounting is not a theorem-proof subject, and this site does not pretend otherwise. It is a
mechanics-first subject: a small set of structural facts — the accounting equation, the
double-entry rule, the accrual principle — generate everything else, and mastery means executing
the mechanics without error and knowing *why* each step is forced.

## The tracks

- **[Foundations](/1-foundations/)** — the accounting equation stated as an invariant,
  double-entry as the rule that preserves it, debits and credits defined by their effect on the
  equation's sides, and the trial balance as the invariant's check.
- **[The Accounting Cycle](/2-the-accounting-cycle/)** — journalising, posting, adjusting
  entries (accruals and deferrals justified by the accrual principle), the adjusted trial
  balance, and the construction of the four statements — every step worked, every number
  traceable.

## The worked-example standard

Every page here carries a fully worked example in which every number is traceable: transaction
to journal entry to ledger to trial balance to statement. The examples are small enough to check
by hand and complete enough to interlock — the income statement feeds retained earnings, which
feeds the balance sheet, which must still balance, and the pages show it balancing.

## The through-line

The single structural fact of the subject is that the accounting equation is an invariant, and
double-entry is the operation that preserves it. Everything else — adjusting entries, closing
entries, statement construction — is bookkeeping around that core, and pages here keep the
invariant visible at each step rather than burying it under procedure.

## Prerequisites

Arithmetic and the patience to check that entries balance. The subject's difficulty is
discipline, not mathematics — and the discipline is easier to keep when the structure explains
the rules, which is the ordering these pages take.

## Corrections and error reporting

A worked example that does not balance is a defect of the worst kind here — it teaches the
mechanic broken. If you find one, it is fixed and the correction recorded. The same goes for
entries that balance but post to the wrong side of the equation: balancing is necessary, not
sufficient, and the corrections hold both standards.

## The exam-board connection

GCSE, A-Level, and IB business syllabi touch the accounting equation and simple statements; the
exam-board sites carry those treatments with their assessment framing. This site is the layer
underneath, where the invariants live, and the cross-references are maintained by tooling.

## The self-test convention

Each page closes with a self-test keyed to its sections. The items are execution-first — predict
the entry, produce the balance, trace the number — because the subject is learned by doing, and
the self-tests are where the doing is checked before it counts.

## Corrections

A worked example that does not balance is a defect of the worst kind here — it teaches the
mechanic broken. If you find one, it is fixed and the correction recorded. The same goes for
entries that balance but post to the wrong side of the equation: balancing is necessary, not
sufficient, and the corrections hold both standards.

## Where the site is going

Foundations and the cycle open the site; management accounting (cost behaviour, budgeting,
variance analysis) is the planned second subject area, built on the same mechanics-first standard
— every variance computed from a source, every standard justified.

## The reading order

[Foundations](/1-foundations/) first, [The Accounting Cycle](/2-the-accounting-cycle/) second —
and the cycle read with a pencil, producing each entry before reading it. The pages are written
so that every produced entry can be checked against the shown one, and the check is where the
learning happens.

## What the site is not

This is not a standards reference: it teaches the mechanics and names the frameworks, but the
authoritative texts are the standards themselves. Where a page simplifies a rule for teaching,
the simplification is flagged — the flag is part of the standard, not an apology for it.

## The one-paragraph version

Assets = Liabilities + Equity always. Every transaction posts equal debits and credits, which is
why the equation holds after every transaction, not just at the end. The trial balance checks
it, adjusting entries keep accrual honesty inside it, and the four statements are reports of it.
That is the subject; the tracks execute it.

## The cycle in one sentence

Journal, post, adjust, check, report, close — and the equation holds at every comma. The tracks
teach each comma, because students who can say that sentence and mean every part of it can run
the subject.

## The self-test order

Predict before you read the shown entry; balance before you read the shown total; trace before
you read the shown statement line. The self-tests are sequenced in exactly that order, and
working them in that order is the difference between reading accounting and doing it.

## Start here

- Begin with [The Accounting Equation and Double Entry](/1-foundations/1_the-accounting-equation/)
  — the invariant, the proof that double entry preserves it through all four entry shapes, and a
  worked example balancing after every event.
- Then [the cycle](/2-the-accounting-cycle/): the same machinery executed across a full period,
  with adjustments justified by the accrual principle and the statements constructed from the
  adjusted trial balance.

## The standard

Definitions precede use. Each mechanic is demonstrated before it is generalised. Every worked
example balances — not as a flourish but as the subject's own verification — and where frameworks
differ, the difference is named. The [study hub](/hub/), [about page](/about/), and
[glossary](/glossary/) carry the details.
